review_notes: I read the whole file and the related sources. I checked that `LinearMap.baseChange` and the tensor-product module structure only need `[Semiring A]`, and I looked at `Basis.linearMap`, `toMatrix` and `trace_baseChange`. `baseChange_linearMap`, `baseChange_end` and `toMatrix_baseChange` need `CommSemiring A`, because `Basis.linearMap`, `Basis.end` and `LinearMap.toMatrix` require a commutative scalar ring. Those three are not over-specialised. The only generalisation I found is `instFree`. I did not compile the proposed change. I expect it to work because the `basis` definition already elaborates in the `Semiring A` section.

findings.excerpt:
[CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] :
    Module.Free A (A ⊗[R] M) :=
findings.problem: `instFree` assumes `[CommSemiring A]`, but nothing in its proof needs commutativity of `A`. It is proved from `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A (Module.Free.chooseBasis R M)`. That `basis` is defined in the same file under `[Semiring A] [Algebra R A]`. `Module.Free A _` and `Module.Free.of_basis` only need a `Semiring A`. The instance therefore does not apply to a noncommutative `R`-algebra `A`, such as a matrix algebra over `R`, even though the basis construction above it does.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `[CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A]` with `[Semiring A] [Algebra R A]` in `instFree`. Keep the proof `Module.Free.of_basis <| Algebra.TensorProduct.basis A (Module.Free.chooseBasis R M)`. The `Module A (A ⊗[R] M)` instance already elaborates in the `Semiring A` section for `basis`, so the statement should elaborate unchanged. The `CommSemiring A` instances remain applicable for commutative `A`, since they supply a `Semiring A`.
findings.benefit: Freeness of the base change becomes available as an instance for noncommutative algebras `A`. This matches the generality of `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis` and the module structure. Existing commutative uses are unaffected, because the commutative instances still supply a `Semiring A`.
